task.description: Hard gate (WF-02 Step 1b, applied here per WF-03's design-review step) on CODE-DESIGNER's iss0226-sandbox-pool-worker-result-typing.md design against ISS-0226's four acceptance criteria.
acceptance_criteria: The worker result has an explicit closed type declared in lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex
handle_info/2 is total over that type
A test drives an unexpected return and asserts the pool survives with slot bookkeeping intact
No change to INV-SP-A1..A3 or owner-monitor reclaim semantics

result.summary: Independently re-read lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex, lib/letflow/design/iss0224-sandbox-pool-async-provisioning.md, and the design doc in full (not the CODE-DESIGNER handoff summary). Every substantive claim in the design checks out against source: run_op/1 (:586-590) has no @spec and complete_op/3 (:597-665) is exactly four exact-match clauses with no catch-all -- a fifth return shape would raise FunctionClauseError inside handle_info/2, a GenServer callback (confirmed by reading both functions directly). The proposed worker_result() union (provision_result() | drop_result()) is byte-for-byte what provision_sandbox/2 (:871-894, returns {:ok, %SandboxClaim{}} or {:error, :provision_failed} via its rescue) and drop_schema/1 (:902-907, returns :ok or {:error, :release_failed} via its rescue) actually return today -- confirmed by reading both bodies. classify_worker_result/2's five-clause design (four legal pairings + catch-all) is genuinely total by construction. Routing :invalid to handle_worker_death/1 (:667-700) is a sound reuse, not a hand-wave: read handle_worker_death/1 directly and confirm its per-op-kind recovery (compensating orphan-drop for a provision, {:error, :release_failed} reply for a release-in-flight, unconditional in_flight clear) is a genuinely correct answer to 'the pool does not know what happened to the DB side effect' -- and confirmed this is the right equivalence class: an unrecognized return and a crash-without-returning are the same uncertainty from the pool's perspective (neither is a legal completion signal), so reusing the exact function clause B case 1 already calls is sound, not merely convenient. The demonitor-before-branching ordering claim in section 4.2 matches the current code's placement exactly (:397, 'flush BEFORE calling complete_op') -- preserving it identically on both branches is correct and necessary to avoid a stray :DOWN(:normal) misread by clause B case 1. Checked INV-SP-A1/A2/A3 (iss0224 design doc lines 1234-1259) and owner-monitor reclaim (:669-700, :702-...) individually against the new design, not against section 8's self-assessment: none of state shape, complete_op/3's four clauses, handle_worker_death/1, or clause B's :DOWN dispatch are modified by this design -- the invariant-preservation argument holds. The test design's :sys.replace_state/2 + fabricated task_ref + send(pool, {fake_ref, garbage}) mechanism is legitimate and deterministic: handle_info({ref, result}, state) when is_reference(ref) matches on ANY two-tuple whose first element is a reference, so a fabricated ref reaches clause A exactly as a real Task's reply would, and because the fake ref is never attached to a real Task there is no race with a genuine worker message. FAIL is for one single, specific, fixable gap: check (e) of WF-02 Step 1b and .claude/agents/code-design-validator.md's explicit prohibition -- 'no real .ex/.exs bodies -- signatures and type shapes only'. Section 4.2 ('New shape') of the design doc is not a signature or algorithm description -- it is a complete, real Elixir function body for the NEW handle_info/2 clause A: a full case statement, a real Logger.error/1 call with string interpolation, real pipe chains (state |> complete_op(...) |> service_next_waiter() |> pump()), and real {:noreply, new_state} returns. Section 6 ('Signatures... design-only -- no implementation bodies') itself concedes this by pointing back to section 4.2 for 'the full new body' rather than restating only a signature there -- an explicit acknowledgement that section 4.2 is a body, not a signature. Per WF-02 Step 1b: 'FAIL immediately on any check failure -- no partial credit', and per core-directives.md's Humanless-operation section, a validator must not rubber-stamp on the strength of the surrounding reasoning being sound -- the prohibition is unconditional regardless of how well-justified the omitted body would be.

issues.description: lib/letflow/design/iss0226-sandbox-pool-worker-result-typing.md section 4.2 ('New shape') contains a complete, real Elixir function body for handle_info/2's new clause A (the full if/else, the case statement over classify_worker_result/2's result, the Logger.error/1 call with its interpolated string, the state |> complete_op(...) |> service_next_waiter() |> pump() pipe chain, and both {:noreply, new_state} returns) -- this is implementation code, not a signature or type shape, and is forbidden by WF-02 Step 1b check (e) and .claude/agents/code-designer.md's 'no function bodies, no actual .ex/.exs code blocks' rule.

correction_instructions: Rewrite section 4.2 to describe the new clause-A body as PROSE/algorithm steps plus the @spec-level signature only -- e.g.: 'after the unconditional Process.demonitor(ref, [:flush]) (unchanged from today), call classify_worker_result(state.in_flight.op, result); on {:ok, validated_result} run the existing complete_op/3 |> service_next_waiter/1 |> pump/1 pipeline unchanged; on :invalid, log the op kind/sandbox_id/raw result via Logger.error/1 then run handle_worker_death/1 |> service_next_waiter/1 |> pump/1 instead' -- keep the totality ARGUMENT (section 4.2's prose paragraph and the 4.3 justification) but delete the literal `def handle_info(...) do ... end` code block.

Section 4.1 ('Current shape') quoting the EXISTING code verbatim as a citation of what is being replaced is not the same defect (it documents current-state fact, not proposed implementation) and may stay, but re-confirm it is clearly labeled as read-only reference, not part of the design's implementation-code count.

Re-run the same no-code check across the rest of the doc (sections 3, 5, 6, 7) before resubmitting -- section 6 is fine (signatures/typespecs only) but double check no other section was written the same way section 4.2 was.

After the fix, the four acceptance criteria and all other content in this design (the closed type, the totality argument, the recovery-mechanism reasoning, the invariant-preservation checklist, the test design) were independently verified sound in this gate's summary above -- no other rework is needed.
result.next_action: Rework CODE-DESIGNER: remove section 4.2's real implementation code block, replace with algorithm prose + signature only, then re-route to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR.
